title: Reliable clonal seed reproduction across major hybrid crops

concept.text: The innovation would let a high-performing hybrid crop reproduce its genetic combination faithfully through seed over successive generations. In ordinary sexual reproduction, genetic reshuffling means seed saved from a hybrid does not reliably reproduce the original hybrid genotype. Synthetic apomixis seeks to bypass that reshuffling and produce clonal offspring through seed. The supplied rice research combines apomeiosis, which avoids the usual chromosome reduction and reshuffling of meiosis, with parthenogenesis, which initiates embryo development without fertilization of the egg.

The proposed capability goes beyond obtaining some clonal rice seedlings: it requires dependable, highly fertile clonal seed production across major crop species, elite hybrid backgrounds, growing conditions and saved-seed generations. It also includes a practical, controlled route back to sexual breeding so breeders can create new genetic combinations. Clonal seed frequency, genome fidelity, fertility, seed quality and crop yield are separate requirements; success on one does not establish the others. This broader target is a synthesis of the supplied concept and review, rather than an achievement demonstrated by the cited experiments.

significance.text: If seed faithfully retained an elite hybrid genotype, farmers and seed producers could multiply that hybrid without reconstructing its parental cross for every seed generation. This could preserve the genetic basis of hybrid vigor while changing how hybrid seed is produced and maintained. Transferability across major crops would make the advance consequential for agricultural breeding and seed multiplication, rather than an improvement confined to one rice system.

As a conditional downstream possibility, reliable clonal seed could make selected hybrid combinations easier to maintain and distribute, while controlled sexual breeding would allow continued development of improved combinations. Genetic preservation would not guarantee identical performance in different environments, higher yield, lower seed prices or widespread adoption. The value of the system would depend on the hybrid being propagated and on the fertility, seed quality and agronomic performance of its clonal descendants.

Access is a separate consideration from biological feasibility. Seed law, ownership arrangements and distribution systems could affect whether farmers can obtain, save and exchange such seed. These are reasonable qualifications to the potential impact, but the supplied evidence does not examine particular legal regimes, commercial arrangements or access outcomes.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central engineering challenge is to make the components of clonal seed formation work together reliably without imposing unacceptable reproductive costs. In the reviewed rice experiment, some engineered lines maintained their reported clonal output while others varied across generations or locations, and every tested line had reduced seed-setting relative to controls. These findings identify stability and fertility as concrete obstacles within that experimental system; they do not show that every synthetic-apomixis system has the same limitations.

For the proposed broader capability, the remaining tasks include transferring the reproductive system among biologically distinct crops and elite genetic backgrounds, maintaining dependable performance across environments and generations, and establishing genome-level fidelity alongside useful seed production and yield. Chromosome number alone cannot establish that offspring faithfully preserve the parental genome, and a high proportion of apparently clonal seedlings does not by itself establish a productive seed crop. These are requirements inferred from the target and the reviewed measurement limitations, not evidence that all routes to satisfying them have been surveyed.

A controlled return to sexual breeding is an additional design requirement: breeders would need to recover viable recombinant offspring when they want new combinations, while retaining reliable clonal reproduction during seed multiplication. The supplied evidence contains no demonstration of this transition and does not establish its present technical status across crops. Likewise, the rice evidence alone cannot establish the global absence of the complete proposed capability.

current_state.text: Synthetic apomixis has been demonstrated in rice. Wang and colleagues’ study, published on 9 February 2026 in Frontiers in Plant Science, examined ten engineered lines in the single hybrid rice background Yongyou 4949. It reported seven lines with stable clonal progeny over the generations examined, one with progressively declining induction across generations, and two whose induction varied between cultivation locations. The supported conclusion is that stability depended on the tested line and conditions, rather than that inheritance was uniformly unstable or uniformly reliable.

The study assessed clonal progeny principally through ploidy measurements and also reported preservation of morphological characteristics. These observations support the authors’ reported outcome within their assay scope, but they are not independent genome-wide verification of clone fidelity. All tested engineered lines had significantly reduced seed-setting relative to the wild-type control, whose reported seed-setting rate was 94.39%. Thus, reported clonal induction and reproductive productivity must be assessed separately.

The two location-sensitive lines were identified as HW14 and CL6. Their site-associated variation was reported in the article text; the proposed explanation involving environmental effects, including temperature, remains tentative. Inconsistent wording in parts of the results was resolved in the supplied review by reference to the abstract and the more detailed stability results. The retained article text was available to that review, but figure images and supplementary materials were not inspected, limiting assessment of details available only in those materials.

The reconciled research separately cites Meynard, Vernet and colleagues’ “Apomeiosis circumvents sterility in inter-subspecific hybrids of rice,” listed as first published on 28 June 2026 in The Plant Journal. It attributes two findings to the paper: that apomeiosis could overcome sterility in those hybrids, and that achieving fertility together with apomixis required further optimization. No source text or retained artifact for this citation was supplied to the review, so its identity, date and attributed findings could not be independently checked within this evidence set. The attribution is preserved as an unverified research lead; the lack of captured evidence does not establish that the reported result is false.

The supplied evidence establishes dated progress in one rice hybrid background, not completion across major crops or a demonstrated route back to sexual breeding. No freshness-search record was supplied, so the material cannot establish a comprehensive state of the field as of 1 November 2026 or exclude subsequent advances. That coverage limitation does not invalidate the supported February 2026 findings.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: establish reliable clonal seed reproduction in several biologically distinct major crops and multiple elite hybrid backgrounds. Compare engineered plants and their descendants with appropriate hybrid controls, using practical performance thresholds specified before testing. The crop selection and thresholds would need justification for the intended uses; they are proposed evaluation choices, not published consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Clonal reproduction meets thresholds across major crops and elite hybrids

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: independently measure genome-level clone fidelity, the fraction of clonal offspring, fertility, seed-setting, seed quality and crop yield across multiple locations and successive saved-seed generations. Report line-specific results, variability and failures so that a strong average does not obscure an unreliable background or environment. The reviewed rice study directly motivates extended environmental and generational testing, although it does not prescribe this full evaluation framework.
completion_criteria.label: Clonal fidelity and crop performance measured across locations and generations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and breeding tests: have independent groups reproduce the core fertility and fidelity results, and demonstrate a controlled transition to sexual breeding that yields viable recombinant offspring. Define the crops, backgrounds, environments and generations for which performance is demonstrated, together with practical limits on seed multiplication and use. Even extensive finite testing would establish breadth within those boundaries, rather than literal universality across all crops and conditions.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication and viable sexual recombinants within defined performance limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AGR-01, “Cereal crops supplied predominantly by biological nitrogen fixation,” and AGR-02, “A transferable carbon-concentrating system for C3 staple crops,” share the challenge of transferring complex biological functions into useful crop backgrounds. Their targets are nutrient supply and photosynthetic performance; AGR-03 concerns inheritance and reproduction. Clonal seed could help maintain a successful engineered hybrid carrying such traits, but would not create or validate those functions.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-04, “High-yield perennial versions of the major grain-crop portfolio,” changes crop lifespan and regrowth, while AGR-03 changes how a genotype is transmitted through seed. AGR-07, “A general, rapid method for creating productive crops from wild plants,” concerns creating useful crops from wild starting material. Reliable clonal seed might help preserve selected combinations produced through either effort, but neither perenniality nor rapid domestication follows from apomixis.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-05, “Productive staple farming with seawater and a closed salt balance,” AGR-06, “Rapidly programmable, durable crop immunity,” and AGR-09, “Food crops that reliably build durable, additional soil carbon,” target salinity and salt management, disease protection, and soil-carbon outcomes respectively. AGR-03 could potentially preserve hybrid genotypes developed for those purposes. Faithful inheritance alone would establish none of their environmental, immunity or carbon-performance claims.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-08, “Economically accessible, end-to-end autonomous field farming,” addresses farm operations and economics rather than plant reproductive biology. The two innovations could coexist in a farming system, but autonomous cultivation does not establish reliable clonal seed production, and clonal reproduction does not establish operational autonomy or affordability.

unresolved_issues: The Wiley citation’s identity, publication date and attributed fertility and apomixis findings remain unverified within the supplied evidence.
Genome-wide fidelity beyond the reviewed ploidy and morphological assessments remains unestablished by this evidence set.
The causes of location-sensitive induction, including any temperature mechanism, remain tentative.
The demonstrated stability and fertility findings cannot be generalized from Yongyou 4949 to other rice backgrounds or major crops.
The feasibility and current status of controlled return to sexual breeding are not established by the supplied sources.
No freshness-search record establishes comprehensive coverage as of 1 November 2026 or excludes subsequent advances.
Practical thresholds, crop coverage and trial duration for the proposed completion demonstrations remain to be specified.
Specific legal, ownership, distribution and economic consequences are not examined by the supplied evidence.

brief.title: Seeds that faithfully copy high-performing crops
possible: Farmers could save seed from a high-performing hybrid—a crop bred by crossing parents—and grow descendants that retain its genetic combination. This would work reliably across major crops and successive seed generations.
Breeders could keep multiplying a successful combination through seed, then deliberately return to sexual breeding when they want to create new combinations.
why: Farmers and seed producers could multiply successful hybrids without repeating the parental cross for every seed generation. This could preserve the genetic basis of hybrid vigor, the performance advantage a hybrid has over its parents, and make selected combinations easier to maintain and distribute.

sources.showed: In a single rice hybrid, some engineered lines produced genetically matching offspring consistently across the generations studied. Others declined or varied between locations. All tested engineered lines produced seed less successfully than the control.
sources.quote: seven apomictic lines maintained stable clonal progeny
sources.cited_for: The rice results show progress toward copying hybrids through seed, alongside problems with reliability and seed production.
sources.not_established: They do not establish complete genetic fidelity, dependable crop performance across major crops, or a controlled return to sexual breeding.

sources.showed: This study concerns bypassing the usual chromosome reduction and reshuffling to overcome sterility in rice hybrids.
sources.cited_for: The work concerns the fertility component needed for reliable reproduction through seed.
sources.not_established: Overcoming hybrid sterility alone does not establish fertile seed production that faithfully copies the parent.

shown: Wang and colleagues reported that seven engineered lines in a single rice hybrid maintained stable production of clonal offspring—genetic copies—over the generations studied. Other lines declined or varied between locations.

All tested engineered lines had reduced seed production relative to the control. Chromosome counts and plant appearance supported the reported copying, but did not establish fidelity across the entire genetic makeup.
missing: Reliable copying through seed still needs demonstration across biologically distinct major crops and elite hybrids.
Complete genetic fidelity must accompany useful fertility, seed quality and yield across locations and saved-seed generations.
Independent groups must reproduce the core fertility and genetic fidelity results.
A controlled return to sexual breeding must produce viable offspring with new genetic combinations.

milestones.label: Reliable seed copying across major crops and elite hybrids
milestones.explanation: Several distinct major crops and multiple elite hybrids would have to meet practical performance thresholds set before testing, against suitable controls. This would establish useful breadth beyond a single rice hybrid.

milestones.label: Genetic fidelity and crop performance persist across growing conditions
milestones.explanation: Independent measurements would have to establish genetic fidelity, clonal offspring frequency, fertility, seed production, seed quality and yield across locations and generations. Results for each line would reveal unreliable performance.

milestones.label: Independent replication and a controlled return to sexual breeding
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to reproduce fertility and fidelity results and obtain viable sexual offspring with new genetic combinations. Defined performance limits would establish where seed multiplication and breeding work.

uncertain: The causes of location-sensitive copying remain unclear, including whether temperature affects the process.
The feasibility of a controlled return to sexual breeding remains unresolved.
Practical performance thresholds, crop coverage and the duration of trials remain to be defined.

page.title: Synthetic apomixis across hybrid crops
page.definition: Synthetic apomixis is engineered production of seed whose embryos preserve the maternal genotype. Hybrids of rice, sorghum, cowpea, pearl millet and Indian mustard can be multiplied through saved seed while retaining the original hybrid’s yield and seed quality.

goal.need: ACIAR’s August 1997 appraisal reported hybrid-rice yields 15–20% above elite inbred lines and hybrid seed costing 10 times ordinary rice seed. Sexual reproduction separates parental gene combinations, requiring repeated production of F1 seed, the first generation of a parental cross. Clonal seed reproduction would preserve those combinations during seed multiplication. These quantities describe the appraisal’s historical setting.

figures.caption: Hybrid-rice quantities in ACIAR’s August 1997 appraisal.
figures.note: Historical figures reported by the appraisal, not current prices or universal hybrid advantages.

completion.title: Saved hybrid seed preserves genotype, yield and quality in all five target crops.
completion.criterion: In rice, sorghum, cowpea, pearl millet and Indian mustard, farmers can harvest and replant seed from an engineered hybrid through successive seed generations, preserving its maternal hybrid genotype without loss of crop yield or seed quality relative to the original F1 hybrid under farming conditions. This is an Atlas operationalization of the programmes’ seed-saving goals. The sources located prescribe no shared numerical tolerance, minimum generation count or required number of environments.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of the named crop programmes’ goals; no external cross-crop acceptance test was located.
completion.basis: Searched ACIAR, Hy-Gain and UC Davis programme documents and rice/sorghum engineering papers for a cross-crop acceptance standard covering clonal purity, yield, generations and environments. None specifies one. This test retains the programmes’ seed-saving goal and the developers’ prerequisites of clonal inheritance and preserved crop performance; it adds no numerical tolerances.

milestones.title: A crop produces unreduced gametes that retain its parental genotype.
milestones.criterion: Apomeiosis produces viable gametes retaining parental chromosome number and allele combinations; MiMe achieves this by replacing meiosis with one mitotic-like division. Laboratory precedent: Arabidopsis yielded 24/24 tetraploid selfed progeny, reported on 9 June 2009. Rice: apomeiosis restored fertility in two indica/japonica hybrids normally showing 5.5% and 55% grain filling, reported on 28 June 2026. Sorghum: MiMe was engineered in Tx430.
milestones.set_by: Plant reproductive genetics convention: the MiMe phenotype defined by d’Erfurth et al. and subsequently implemented in crop studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: The obtained plants produce functional diploid gametes that are genetically identical to their mother.

milestones.title: A crop egg develops into an embryo without fertilization.
milestones.criterion: An egg forms an embryo without fertilization, the field’s definition of parthenogenesis. Pearl millet: three transgenic lines formed embryos in 35–36% of mature embryo sacs, with 82, 169 and 76 sacs examined, reported on 24 August 2015. Rice: BBM1 expression produced embryos in 12/98 emasculated pistils nine days after emasculation, reported online on 12 December 2018. Seed maturation can still require fertilization of the endosperm, the tissue nourishing the embryo.
milestones.set_by: Plant reproductive biology convention, defined and experimentally tested by Conner et al. in pearl millet and Khanday et al. in rice.

milestones.title: Clonal seed production, genotype and agronomic traits persist across saved-seed generations.
milestones.criterion: Clonal induction, agronomic traits and genetic/epigenetic integrity persist across seed generations; no generation count is prescribed. Rice: genome sequencing supported inheritance in 6 T1 and 18 T2 descendants of two transformants, reported on 27 December 2022. On 9 February 2026, seven of ten Yongyou 4949 lines were stable by ploidy through T3 at two locations; all ten had reduced seed set, sampled at 4–5 plants/line. Sorghum event 143 maintained apomixis through T4 with reduced seed production; SNP samples comprised 207 T2, 638 T3 and 126 T4 plants.
milestones.set_by: Wang et al., Hainan University and State Key Laboratory of Hybrid Rice, Introduction; a published research milestone stated for rice and also investigated in sorghum.
milestones.threshold_quote: This multi-generational stability represents a critical milestone for the practical application of apomixis technology in crop improvement programs.

milestones.title: A hybrid crop approaches 100% clonal seed production while retaining hybrid seed yield.
milestones.criterion: Clonal seed production approaches 100% while seed yield remains comparable to sexually produced hybrids, as required by Simon et al.; no numerical meaning for “near” or yield-equivalence margin is specified. Rice: ten Yongyou 4949 lines produced 95.3–100% diploid progeny with 80.7–86.7% seed set in T1, reported on 26 November 2024. Diploidy screens chromosome number and does not establish genome fidelity. Sorghum’s two published engineered hybrids retained reduced seed yields.
milestones.set_by: Corteva Agriscience–University of Queensland developers, Simon et al., Introduction; an agricultural prerequisite drawn from the synthetic-apomixis literature.
milestones.threshold_quote: Seed yield comparable to sexually produced hybrids and near 100% penetrance of clonal seed is required

milestones.title: Field-grown clonal descendants retain the original hybrid’s traits and hybrid vigour.
milestones.criterion: Clonal descendants retain hybrid traits and performance under field conditions. Rice Fix8 #3 had diploid T2 frequencies of 1,101/1,104, 1,176/1,180 and 804/806; mean field seed set was 76.8–79.4% versus 77.3–80.7% in controls, reported on 21 July 2026. These comparisons assess seed set and yield components, without a prespecified equivalence margin. Sorghum: OGTR authorised a one-site trial of at most 1 ha on 6 March 2025; that licence supplies no efficacy result.
milestones.set_by: CIRAD–UC Davis–Max Planck developers, Vernet et al., Discussion; a field-validation criterion stated for rice.
milestones.threshold_quote: Trueness-to-type and hybrid vigor should ultimately be evaluated under a field trial to confirm greenhouse findings.

not_found: No cross-crop acceptance standard specifying clonal purity, yield equivalence, generation count and environmental coverage was located.
Searches located no published synthetic-apomixis milestone results for cowpea or Indian mustard, or complete synthetic apomixis in pearl millet.
Meynard et al.’s publisher abstract and publication date were accessible, but its full text could not be opened.
No externally specified completion test requiring a controlled return from synthetic apomixis to sexual breeding was located.

results.finding: Seven of ten engineered hybrid rice lines maintained stable diploid induction across generations.
results.detail: Ploidy was used as a proxy for clonal induction; genetic and epigenetic integrity were not established. All lines had reduced seed set, and three showed unstable induction.
results.quote: By analyzing progeny clonal seeds frequency across generations and locations, we demonstrated that seven apomictic lines maintained stable clonal progeny, while one progressively declined across generations.

results.finding: Rice line HW7 reached 100% diploid induction across sampled generations.
results.detail: Seed set was consistently low, and all ten lines had significantly reduced seed set versus the control. Diploidy alone does not establish genome fidelity; seed-set sampling used 4–5 plants per line.
results.quote: In contrast, line HW7 maintained high and stable induction rates (90.23% to 100%) but consistently low seed-setting rates (38.96%, 35.73%, 33.24%)

results.finding: All ten field-grown rice lines had significantly reduced seed set versus the 94.39% control.
results.detail: Plants were sampled across generations at 4–5 plants per line. The study reports preserved morphology, but reduced seed set falls short of establishing retained hybrid performance.
results.quote: All lines exhibited significantly reduced seed-setting rates compared to the wild-type control (94.39%).

results.finding: Hybrid rice MiMe mutants: all 109 progeny from four events were tetraploid.
results.detail: Tetraploid progeny indicate fusion of unreduced gametes. Whole-genome sequencing of separate MiMe plus BBM1 lines showed retention of the hybrid genotype in all 24 sequenced T1 and T2 progeny.
results.quote:

results.finding: In Tx623/Tx430 hybrid sorghum, 229 of 238 MiMe progeny retained heterozygosity across all chromosomes.
results.detail: Diploid clonal progeny demonstrate viable unreduced female gametes; hybrid tetraploid progeny indicate MiMe activity in both male and female gametes. Nine progeny showed evidence of aneuploidy.

results.finding: Rice egg cells co-expressing OsWOX9A and OsBBM1 showed 86–91% parthenogenesis; sample size not stated.
results.quote: Co-expression of OsWOX9A and OsBBM1 in egg cells results in 86-91% parthenogenesis, representing 4- to 15-fold increases over OsBBM1 alone.

results.finding: In 44 transgenic Tx430 sorghum plants examined, three constructs induced average parthenogenesis rates above 40%.
results.detail: The 44 plants covered all six constructs tested; the source does not state the sample size for the three higher-rate constructs in the supplied text. Fertilization was prevented by removing stigmas before anthesis.

results.finding: Transgenic pearl millet: parthenogenesis occurred in 35–36% of mature embryo sacs across three lines (82, 169 and 76 sacs examined).
results.detail: Heads were bagged and stigmas and styles removed to prevent fertilization. Embryos were observed two days after anthesis.
results.quote: Parthenogenesis ranged from 35% to 36% in lines g11a, g52, and g3f, whereas the untransformed offspring showed no parthenogenesis.

results.finding: Hybrid rice maintained clonal traits through T4; 11 of 345 T3 progeny were diploid.
results.detail: Agronomic traits, genome and methylation were stable in selected clonal descendants. Seed set was reduced to 5.7%–7%, and rare aneuploid offspring had genomic deletions.
results.quote: By analyzing agronomic traits, as well as the genome, methylome, transcriptome, and allele-specific transcriptome, we showed that the descendant clonal plants remained stable.

results.finding: Hybrid rice: all 24 sequenced T1 and T2 descendants retained the parental heterozygous genotype.
results.detail: Clonal induction and most measured traits persisted across generations, but grain filling was significantly reduced compared with the F1 control. Plants were grown in a greenhouse; field performance and epigenetic integrity were not directly tested.
results.quote: In contrast, all the T0, T1, and T2 plants retained the heterozygous parental genotype in the entire genome, showing that they are completely clonal.

results.finding: Sorghum event 143 retained heterozygous SNP markers across all chromosomes in 97% of 126 T4 progeny.
results.detail: Apomixis and reduced seed set persisted across generations. Some progeny were aneuploid; grain weight and germination were reduced relative to controls. SNP markers assessed genetic inheritance, but epigenetic integrity was not reported.

results.finding: In one Fix8_P2 hybrid rice line, 673 of 679 progeny were diploid, reported as 99.1% clonal efficiency.
results.detail: Seed set was 80.3% versus 78.3% in the F1 control. The paper claims comparable seed yields but reports seed set rather than a direct seed-yield measurement for this comparison. Large-scale screening used diploidy as a proxy for clonality.
results.quote: Among 679 and 766 progeny, we identified 673 and 760 diploid individuals, corresponding to clonal efficiencies of 99.1% and 99.2%, respectively.

results.finding: Ten Yongyou 4949 hybrid rice lines produced 95.3%–100.0% diploid progeny.
results.detail: T1 seed set was 80.7%–86.7%, but seed yield was not directly compared with the sexually produced hybrid. Diploidy is a proxy for clonal reproduction and does not by itself establish genome fidelity.

Among the 59 apomictic lines, 10 lines (lines K18, K20, K22, K31, K35, K48, K51, K58, K64, and K65) produced 95.3%–100.0% diploid progeny which showed seed-setting rates of >80.0% (80.7%–86.7%) in T
1

results.finding: Field-grown Fix8 #3 rice T2 populations (n=3,090) had mean seed set of 76.8–79.4%.
results.detail: Three T2 populations were screened for ploidy; seed set was measured in selected plants. Field controls had 77.3–80.7% seed set. Comparisons covered seed set and yield components, without a prespecified equivalence margin.
